To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have performed Coulomb Dissociations on the stable isotopes of molydbenum 92Mo,94Mo,100Mo, and the unstable isotope of molydbenem 93Mo at the R3B-LAND setup at GSI.
the Coulomb Dissociations of 92,93 and 94Mo were measured for the first time.
we have measured the Coulomb Dissociations of stable 92,94 and 100Mo as well as the unstable 93Mo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of the stable isotopic chains of Mo and Ru in the p-nucleosynthesis process, which is a crucial test for the astrophysical models of the p-process.
the study of nuclear reactions induced by charged particles, which are relevant for the astrophysical p-process.
the study of the production of p-isotopes in the s-process and the p-process of nucleosynthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Coulomb Dissociated data are in very good agreement with the photon data.
the experimental cross sections of the (g,n)-reactions of the Mo-isotopes are well reproduced by the TALYS model.
the Coulomb dissociation is a very powerful tool for the measurement of (g,n) cross sections, especially in the region of the p-nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Coulomb Dissociations of the stable Mo isotopic chains have been studied and a new result for the 93Mo(g;n) reaction has been obtained.
the CD method is a very promising technique to study (g,n) reaction cross sections.
the Coulomb Dissociated cross sections of the 92Mo(g,n), 94Mo(g.n) and 100Mo(g,n)) reactions are in good agreement (within a factor of 2-3) with the theoretical predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Coulomb Dissociations are a viable method to measure the cross sections for the reactions of interest.
the Coulomb Dissociations of the 92Mo, 94Mo and 100Mo reactions are in good agreement to the corresponding (g,n) reaction cross sections.
the (g,n)-reactions of the stable isotopic molybdenums are not able to explain the underproduction of these elements in the p-process nucleosynthetic model.
